Definition: Columns correspond closely with terms listed on page 34 of www.ensembl.org/info/docs/tools/vep/script/VEP_script_documentation.pdf
Reference: https://bbmap.org/tools/bbsplit
Sample identifier.
The chromosome in which the variant occurs
The position in which the variant occurs. Coordinates map to REFERENCE_GENOME.
Reference Allele in REFERENCE_GENOME
Alternate Allele that occurs in place of the reference allele in the tumor sample

Typically, only PASS variants are added to the excel report. These are variants that pass Mutect2's probability filters. For more info please see: https://github.com/broadinstitute/gatk/blob/master/docs/mutect/mutect.pdf
This is a CCG computed column.  TRUE if BIOTYPE = protein_coding AND (gnomAD_e <= 0.01 OR (gnomADe_AF <= 0.10 AND is in the COSMIC_v104 database) AND AF > 0.02
This is a CCG computed column. Indicates if the variant passes the filtering criteria used in the Variant_Summary_table tab
Type of variant: SNV, Indel, MNV (Multi-Nucleotide Variant).
The gene symbol or name based on the BestEffect (most severely affected) transcript
The database from which the gene symbol or name is derived. HGNC is the HUGO Gene Nomenclature Committee
The ID number for the Gene in the HGNC Database.
The ID number for the Gene in the Ensemble Database.
The biological category of transcript (e.g. protein_coding, LncRNA, miRNA, others).
The effect for the given variant across the standard/most common transcript.
If the standard/most common transcript of the variant is in an exon, this will have the 'Exon number / Number of total exons'
If the standard/most common transcript of the variant is in an intron, this will have the 'Intron number / Number of total introns'
Relative position of the base pair from the start of the mature, standard, most common transcript (cDNA) sequence.
The standardized HGVS Nomenclature describing the variant relative to the start codon (Coding DNA Sequence (CDS) position) in the standard/most common transcript.
The standardized HGVS Nomenclature describing the ascertained protein consequence from the standard/most common transcript.
The effect for the given variant across the most severely affected transcript.
If the most severely affected transcript of the variant is in an exon, this will have the 'Exon number / Number of total exons'
If the most severely affected transcript of the variant is in an intron, this will have the 'Intron number / Number of total introns'
Relative position of the base pair from the start of the mature, most severely affected transcript (cDNA) sequence.
The standardized HGVS Nomenclature describing the variant relative to the start codon (Coding DNA Sequence (CDS) position) in the most severely affected transcript.
The standardized HGVS Nomenclature describing the ascertained protein consequence from the most severely affected transcript.
Allele Fraction from Mutect2. Mutect2 filters out putative contaminating reads from normal tissue.
Depth from Mutect2. Mutect2 filters out putative contaminating reads from normal tissue.

The IDs in the following databases that catalogue known variants: dbSNP (start with rs), HGMD (start with CM (Missense/Nonsense), CD (Deletion), or CI (Insertion)). Further information on databases in the VEP cache is here: https://jun2026.archive.ensembl.org/info/genome/variation/species/sources_documentation.html.
The ID from COSMIC (catalogue of somatic mutations in cancer) version 104. COSV IDs are mapped to one and only one chromosome, position, and variant.
Number of times this COSMIC_v104 ID was found in whole genome screens.
Number of times this COSMIC_v104 ID was found in targeted panels.
The ID from COSMIC (catalogue of somatic mutations in cancer) version 80. COSM IDs are less consistent than COSV IDs (mapped sometimes by variant and sometimes by RNA transcript).
Number of times this COSMIC_v104 ID was found in any screen.
Frequency of existing variant in 1000 Genomes. This is a renamed column; it corresponds to the AF column in the CSQ section of the .vcf file.
Frequency of existing variant in gnomAD exomes combined population
Frequency of existing variant in gnomAD genomes combined population
Maximum observed allele frequency in 1000 Genomes, ESP and gnomAD
Populations (African/American, Ashkenazi Jewish, East Asian, South Asian, etc.) in which maximum allele frequency was observed.
If True, the variant was seen in the HAMAs (Human genome Aligned Mouse Alleles) list. This is in case there is a variant that makes it past bbsplit.
Number of reads aligned/assigned to the primary genome (REFERENCE_GENOME). This is the sum of all Illumina lanes for the sample. Alias is the assignedReads column in bbsplit.
Number of reads aligned/assigned to the mouse genome. These are filtered out by bbsplit. This is the sum of all Illumina lanes for the sample. Alias is the assignedReads column in bbsplit.
Total reads to both mouse and human genome. The bbsplit tool runs after FastQC and FastP but before alignment and deduplication.
Calculated from bbsplit data: (NCBIM37 reads / total reads) * 100

Human genome-Aligned Mouse Alleles (HAMAs) (Jo, et al. 2019. Genome Biology.) found by Mutect2 from the mouse positive controls. These are used as a secondary, blacklisted filter in case there are mouse-strain specific alleles that make it past bbsplit.
